checks.title: Session cookies set without HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite
checks.expected_secure_behavior: Session and authentication cookies are issued with HttpOnly, Secure and an explicit SameSite attribute.
checks.remediation: Set httpOnly:true, secure:true and sameSite:'lax' or 'strict' on session cookies (SESSION_COOKIE_* in Flask/Django); never write session cookies from JavaScript.

checks.title: DOM XSS sinks fed with non-literal input
checks.expected_secure_behavior: Untrusted data reaches the DOM/HTTP response only through text-safe APIs (textContent, htmlspecialchars/Encode.forHtml, framework auto-escaping) or after sanitisation with a vetted library. Every operand of the markup (concatenation or template) must be a literal, a number, an escaped/sanitised value, a translation/icon/skeleton helper called with only literal arguments, a const bound to a literal or a lookup in a literal table; otherwise the sink is reported. PHP/Java/JSP: echo/print/response-writer output (and HTML strings) fed by request data ($_GET/$_POST/$_REQUEST/$_COOKIE, request.getParameter, annotated parameters) without an HTML-encoding call is reported; Svelte {@html} and EJS <%- %> are treated like v-html. Python (Flask/Django/FastAPI/aiohttp/tornado/http.server): request-derived data (request.args/form/values/json/cookies/headers/data, request.GET/POST/COOKIES/META, route-handler parameters, Query/Path/Body parameters) must not reach render_template_string/Template().render/from_string as template source, Markup()/mark_safe(), an HTML string returned or written by the handler (HttpResponse/make_response/HTMLResponse/wfile.write/return) without escape()/format_html/bleach; Jinja environments are created with autoescape enabled; `{{ x|safe }}` is not applied to request-derived context values. TypeScript/JavaScript: Angular bypassSecurityTrustHtml/Script on non-literal values (and [innerHTML] bound to data a component marks trusted), res.send/res.write of HTML strings that interpolate req.body/query/params, template-engine compile of request data (ejs/pug/nunjucks/handlebars) and jQuery .html() of browser-controlled data (location/document sources) are reported.
checks.remediation: Use textContent/framework interpolation, or pass HTML through DOMPurify.sanitize() before innerHTML, dangerouslySetInnerHTML or v-html.

checks.title: Debug mode enabled in production code or configuration
checks.expected_secure_behavior: Production builds run with debug/development mode disabled so stack traces and interactive consoles are never exposed.
checks.remediation: Set DEBUG=False / NODE_ENV=production in deployed configuration and drive any debug flag from environment settings that default to off.

checks.title: Permissive CORS with wildcard or reflected origin and credentials
checks.expected_secure_behavior: Credentialed cross-origin requests are allowed only for an explicit allowlist of trusted origins.
checks.remediation: Replace wildcard/reflected origins with a fixed allowlist, or disable credentials; never echo the Origin header without validating it.

checks.title: Command and code injection sinks built from dynamic strings
checks.expected_secure_behavior: Commands are executed with argument vectors (execFile, subprocess list form, ProcessBuilder without a shell) and no input is passed to eval or Function. Command/code strings that local dataflow proves constant (literals, constants, closed literal collections, shlex.quote-d/escapeshellarg-d arguments for shell sinks) are not reported; CI helper scripts under .github/ are out of scope. PHP: eval/system/exec/shell_exec/passthru/popen/proc_open/backticks and Java: Runtime.exec/ProcessBuilder (with a shell or concatenated string), ScriptEngine.eval are reported when fed by request data or concatenated with a non-constant operand. Python: os.system/os.popen/subprocess.* (shell=True or a command string), asyncio shell sinks, os.exec*/spawn*, eval/exec/compile and pickle/yaml.load (unsafe loader) are reported when the command/code/bytes derive from request data (Flask/Django/FastAPI request sources or route-handler parameters) and are not passed through shlex.quote/int()/an allow-list or closed-set membership check. TypeScript/JavaScript: child_process exec/execSync (and spawn/execFile with shell:true or sh -c), eval/new Function/vm.runIn*/expression evaluators (mathjs.eval) and unserialize are reported when req.body/query/params, handler parameters, NestJS @Body/@Query/@Param values or AWS-Lambda events reach them through same-function dataflow.
checks.remediation: Use execFile/spawn or subprocess.run([...]) without a shell, validate arguments against an allowlist and remove eval/new Function.

checks.title: SQL statements built by string concatenation or interpolation
checks.expected_secure_behavior: Database queries use parameterised statements or an ORM; user input is never concatenated into SQL text. Interpolated fragments are acceptable only when local dataflow proves them non-attacker-controlled (literal constants, conditionals of literals, literal-dict lookups, column names from a closed set, catalog-derived quoted identifiers, identifiers in DDL/PRAGMA/TRIGGER statements that come from a quoted/validated identifier helper, an already-compiled SQL string wrapped in a subquery with params bound separately, or a line carrying an explicit noqa S608/nosec acknowledgement); values must be bound parameters. PHP (mysql_query/mysqli_query/->query) and Java (Statement.execute*/createQuery/createNativeQuery/prepareStatement/JdbcTemplate) sinks are reported when the statement carries request-derived data or an SQL literal concatenated/String.format-ed with a non-constant, non-numeric operand. Python: cursor.execute/executemany/executescript, engine/connection.execute, sqlalchemy text(), Model.objects.raw/extra, RawSQL and pandas read_sql are reported when an SQL literal is combined (f-string, %, .format, +, also through a local variable) with request-derived data, or with a plain function argument in a value position (quoted/after a comparison operator/VALUES/LIKE/IN; identifier positions such as table or column names are not reported); closed-set/validated/int-cast values and bound parameters are not. TypeScript/JavaScript: query/execute/raw/whereRaw/sequelize.query/knex.raw/pool.query/client.query statements and Mongo $where expressions built by template literal or concatenation from req.body/query/params (same-function dataflow) are reported; a function argument is reported only for a db/pool/client receiver with an SQL literal in a value position, and never through sanitize*/escape* helpers.
checks.remediation: Switch to placeholders/prepared statements (cursor.execute(sql, params), $1 bindings) and allowlist any dynamic identifiers.

checks.title: TLS certificate verification disabled
checks.expected_secure_behavior: Outbound TLS connections validate certificate chains and hostnames.
checks.remediation: Remove verify=False / rejectUnauthorized:false / NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0; install the proper CA bundle for private CAs instead.

checks.title: Weak password hashing or insecure randomness for tokens
checks.expected_secure_behavior: Passwords are stored with a slow adaptive KDF (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2) and tokens come from a CSPRNG.
checks.remediation: Hash passwords with bcrypt/Argon2id and generate tokens with secrets.token_urlsafe or crypto.randomBytes instead of Math.random/random.

checks.title: Open redirect driven by request parameter
checks.expected_secure_behavior: Redirect targets come from a server-side allowlist or are validated as same-site relative paths.
checks.remediation: Map user input to known destinations or validate with url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme / a strict relative-path check before redirecting.

checks.title: CSRF protection disabled or exempted
checks.expected_secure_behavior: State-changing endpoints enforce anti-CSRF tokens or equivalent same-site protections.
checks.remediation: Re-enable the framework CSRF middleware and remove blanket exemptions; secure webhook endpoints with signature verification instead.

checks.title: Session is invalidated server-side after logout
checks.expected_secure_behavior: After logout the old session token is rejected by the server and cannot be replayed.
checks.remediation: Destroy the server-side session (or revoke the token) on logout and verify replay of the old token returns 401.

checks.title: File upload validation (type, size, storage location)
checks.expected_secure_behavior: Uploads are validated for content type, size and name, stored outside the web root, and never executed.
checks.remediation: Enforce allowlisted types by content sniffing, size limits, randomised storage names and non-executable storage.

checks.title: Login rate limiting and account lockout
checks.expected_secure_behavior: Repeated failed logins are throttled or locked out and cannot be brute-forced.
checks.remediation: Add per-account and per-IP throttling with progressive delays, lockout or CAPTCHA and alerting on credential stuffing.
